authority: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618 syllabus, 2027-2029, Version 2

records.resolution: Adds direct CORE teaching, practice and assessment for translating both flowcharts and structured-English designs into equivalent Cambridge pseudocode.
Teaches constant initialisation, variable declarations, assignment, arithmetic and logical expressions, keyboard input and console output as connected pseudocode statements.
States the official boundary that functions outside the guide are provided and string manipulation routines are always supplied, so no unofficial substring signature is required from memory.
Provides complete IF/ELSE/nested IF, CASE, count-controlled, pre-condition and post-condition loop teaching, practice and direct assessment evidence.
Requires the loop choice to be justified from known count, possible zero iterations or mandatory first execution rather than from superficial preference.
Defines when a procedure is appropriate and covers no, one or multiple parameters passed by value and by reference with persistent caller effects.
Defines when a function is appropriate and shows its returned value replacing the call inside an expression.
Directly relates procedure/function header, interface, parameter, argument and return value using both definitions and calls.
Confirms clear and efficient Cambridge pseudocode teaching, practice and two independent assessment forms.
Replaces Java-first or unstated-function questions with direct design translation, supplied-routine and loop-choice assessment while preserving all assessment counts and marks.
Maps procedure, function, BYREF/BYVAL and interface terminology to questions that actually assess those concepts instead of unrelated CASE evidence.
Replaces the memorised LEFT/RIGHT/MID chart with a deterministic visual explaining that the question supplies the routine name, parameters and position convention.
Replaces the Java-only comparison visual with a deterministic flowchart/structured-English to pseudocode equivalence model.
